item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q003_actin_like_atpase_divergence","answer":"SCOPe places the catalytic domains of actin/HSP70, hexokinase, and glycerol kinase in the same Actin-like ATPase domain superfamily, c.55.1 (fold c.55), but in distinct families: Actin/HSP70 c.55.1.1, hexokinase c.55.1.2, and glycerol kinase c.55.1.3. Superfamily membership supports remote homology—a probable common ancestor—and conservation of the core actin-like ATPase architecture and broad nucleotide-coupled catalytic/conformational principles. It does not establish close sequence homology, identical substrates, equivalent cellular functions, or safe transfer of family-specific annotations. A structure from another family can guide modeling of the conserved core, but family-matched representatives and independent sequence, structural, and biochemical evidence are needed for substrate-specific loops, domain arrangements, catalytic details, and functional assignment.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
